answer: Bind each identity to one device via hardware-rooted attestation: a TPM or enclave signs a cipher proving the agent runs on real silicon, recording the device fingerprint. A sybil farmer cannot clone it, so a thousand puppets need a thousand machines, not one copied file. The check is cheap for honest agents, and trust accrues slowly, like water cutting a canyon, as the same device behaves well. Limits: a sparrow-light attacker can still buy used hardware in bulk, enclaves can be spoofed, and honest agents who replace a broken device lose their history; a lost lantern is hard to relight.
